DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93, Module 3.

Terminal objective

1.0 Without references, DESCRIBE the purpose, construction, and principles of operation for centrifugal pumps. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.v

Enabling objectives

1.1 STATE the purposes of the following centrifugal pump components: DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.v

  • a. Impeller
  • b. Volute
  • c. Diffuser
  • d. Packing
  • e. Lantern Ring
  • f. Wearing ring

1.2 Given a drawing of a centrifugal pump, IDENTIFY the following major components: DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.v

  • a. Pump casing
  • b. Pump shaft
  • c. Impeller
  • d. Volute
  • e. Stuffing box
  • f. Stuffing box gland
  • g. Packing
  • h. Lantern Ring
  • i. Impeller wearing ring
  • j. Pump casing wearing ring

1.3 DEFINE the following terms: DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.v

  • a. Net Positive Suction Head Available
  • b. Cavitation
  • c. Gas binding
  • d. Shutoff head
  • e. Pump runout

1.4 STATE the relationship between net positive suction head available and net positive suction head required that is necessary to avoid cavitation. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.v

1.5 LIST three indications that a centrifugal pump may be cavitating. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.v

1.6 LIST five changes that can be made in a pump or its surrounding system that can reduce cavitation. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.v

1.7 LIST three effects of cavitation. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.v

1.8 DESCRIBE the shape of the characteristic curve for a centrifugal pump. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.v

1.9 DESCRIBE how centrifugal pumps are protected from the conditions of dead heading and pump runout. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.v

Terminal objective

2.0 Without references, DESCRIBE the purpose, construction, and principle of operation for positive displacement pumps. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.vi

Enabling objectives

2.1 STATE the difference between the flow characteristics of centrifugal and positive displacement pumps. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.vi

2.2 Given a simplified drawing of a positive displacement pump, CLASSIFY the pump as one of the following: DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.vi

  • a. Reciprocating piston pump
  • b. Gear-type rotary pump
  • c. Screw-type rotary pump
  • d. Lobe-type rotary pump
  • e. Moving vane pump
  • f. Diaphragm pump

2.3 EXPLAIN the importance of viscosity as it relates to the operation of a reciprocating positive displacement pump. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.vi

2.4 DESCRIBE the characteristic curve for a positive displacement pump. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.vi

2.5 DEFINE the term slippage. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.vi

2.6 STATE how positive displacement pumps are protected against overpressurization. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.vi

How a centrifugal pump works

Objectives 1.1, 1.2

"Centrifugal pumps basically consist of a stationary pump casing and an impeller mounted on a rotating shaft." DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.1
"The pump casing provides a pressure boundary for the pump and contains channels to properly direct the suction and discharge flow." DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.1

The pump casing guides liquid from the suction connection to the center, or eye, of the impeller. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.1

"The vanes of the rotating impeller impart a radial and rotary motion to the liquid, forcing it to the outer periphery of the pump casing where it is collected in the outer part of the pump casing called the volute." DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.1

The volute expands in cross-sectional area as it wraps around the casing. It collects high velocity liquid from the impeller and gradually reduces fluid velocity by increasing the flow area. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.1

"This converts the velocity head to static pressure." DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.1
"A diffuser is a set of stationary vanes that surround the impeller." DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.3

A diffuser increases efficiency by allowing a more gradual expansion and a less turbulent area for the liquid to reduce in velocity. The growing flow area converts kinetic energy into flow pressure. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.3

Objective 1.1Q1413

What is the purpose of the impeller?

The answer is A. The vanes of the rotating impeller impart a radial and rotary motion to the liquid. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.1

Report a problem
Objective 1.1Q930

What does the volute of a centrifugal pump do?

The answer is B. The volute has a continuously increasing area designed to convert kinetic energy into fluid pressure. DOE-1012-V3 (DOE-HDBK-1012/3-92), Centrifugal Pumps, HT-03 p. 47

Report a problem
Objective 1.1Q1414

What is the purpose of a diffuser in a centrifugal pump?

The answer is B. The purpose of the diffuser is to increase the efficiency of the centrifugal pump by allowing a more gradual expansion and less turbulent area for the liquid to reduce in velocity. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.3

Classifying centrifugal pumps

Objectives 1.0

A single-suction impeller lets liquid enter from one direction, and a double-suction impeller from both sides. Impellers can be open, semi-open, or enclosed. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.3

Pumps are also classified by flow: radial, axial, and mixed. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.4

"In a radial flow pump, the liquid enters at the center of the impeller and is directed out along the impeller blades in a direction at right angles to the pump shaft." DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.4
"In an axial flow pump, the impeller pushes the liquid in a direction parallel to the pump shaft." DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.5

Mixed flow pumps borrow from both: the blades push liquid out from the shaft at an angle greater than 90°. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.6

A single impeller making more than 150 psid is difficult and costly to design, so multiple impellers go on a common shaft in one casing, each discharging to the suction of the next. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.6

"A pump stage is defined as that portion of a centrifugal pump consisting of one impeller and its associated components." DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.6

Centrifugal pump components

Objectives 1.1, 1.2

A small clearance lets the impeller rotate freely in the casing. Liquid leaking through it from discharge to suction lowers efficiency, and erosion slowly widens it. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.7

"Wearing rings are replaceable rings that are attached to the impeller and/or the pump casing to allow a small running clearance between the impeller and the pump casing without causing wear of the actual impeller or pump casing material." DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.8

They are replaced periodically, which prevents the more costly replacement of the impeller or the casing. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.8

"The stuffing box is a cylindrical space in the pump casing surrounding the shaft." DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.9
"Packing is material in the form of rings or strands that is placed in the stuffing box to form a seal to control the rate of leakage along the shaft." DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.9

Packing rings are held by a gland. Tightening the adjusting nuts compresses the packing, which expands radially to form a tight seal. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.9

"Stuffing boxes are normally designed to allow a small amount of controlled leakage along the shaft to provide lubrication and cooling to the packing." DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.9

A standard stuffing box will not work if the suction is under a vacuum or the fluid is too hot to cool the packing. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.9

"A lantern ring is a perforated hollow ring located near the center of the packing box that receives relatively cool, clean liquid from either the discharge of the pump or from an external source and distributes the liquid uniformly around the shaft to provide lubrication and cooling." DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.9
"Mechanical seals consist of two basic parts, a rotating element attached to the pump shaft and a stationary element attached to the pump casing." DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.10

The polished faces of the rotating and stationary elements contact each other to form a seal that prevents leakage along the shaft. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.10

Cavitation and net positive suction head

Objectives 1.3, 1.4

The flow area at the eye of the impeller is usually smaller than the suction piping, so entering liquid speeds up and its pressure drops. The greater the flow, the greater the drop. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.12

"If the pressure drop is large enough, or if the temperature is high enough, the pressure drop may be sufficient to cause the liquid to flash to vapor when the local pressure falls below the saturation pressure for the fluid being pumped." DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.12

Vapor bubbles are swept along the vanes. Where local pressure rises above saturation pressure, they abruptly collapse. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.12

"This process of the formation and subsequent collapse of vapor bubbles in a pump is called" DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.12

That word is cavitation. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.12

"The net positive suction head available (NPSHA) is the difference between the pressure at the suction of the pump and the saturation pressure for the liquid being pumped." DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.12

NPSHA = Psuction - Psaturation DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.13

"The net positive suction head required (NPSHR) is the minimum net positive suction head necessary to avoid cavitation." DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.12
"The condition that must exist to avoid cavitation is that the net positive suction head available must be greater than or equal to the net positive suction head required." DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.13

NPSHA ≥ NPSHR DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.13

When a pump takes suction from a tank, the suction pressure is the absolute pressure at the liquid surface, plus the pressure from elevation, less the friction head losses in the suction line. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.13

NPSHA = Pa + Pst - hf - Psat DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.13

Knowledge check: Cavitation and net positive suction head

Objective 1.3Q38

Cavitation in a pump occurs when:

The answer is A. When local pressure drops below saturation, vapor bubbles form. They collapse as pressure recovers, which damages the impeller. DOE-1018-V1 (DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93), Centrifugal Pump Operation, ME-03 p. 12

Report a problem
Objective 1.3Q340

Net positive suction head (NPSH) is:

The answer is D. NPSH is suction pressure minus the fluid's saturation pressure. DOE-1012-V3 (DOE-HDBK-1012/3-92), Centrifugal Pumps, HT-03 p. 49

Report a problem
Objective 1.4Q1421

What relationship must exist to avoid cavitation?

The answer is D. The net positive suction head available must be greater than or equal to the net positive suction head required. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.13

Report a problem
Objective 1.3Q1422

A pump takes suction from a tank. Pa = 30 ft, Pst = 12 ft, hf = 4 ft, and Psat = 2 ft. What is NPSHA?

The answer is B. NPSHA = Pa + Pst - hf - Psat = 30 + 12 - 4 - 2 = 36 ft. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.13

Report a problem

Recognizing and stopping cavitation

Objectives 1.5, 1.6, 1.7

  • Noise
  • Fluctuating discharge pressure and flow
  • Fluctuating pump motor current

DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.16

"A cavitating pump can sound like a can of marbles being shaken." DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.12
"Other indications that can be observed from a remote operating station are fluctuating discharge pressure, flow rate, and pump motor current." DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.12
  • Degraded pump performance
  • Excessive pump vibration
  • Damage to pump impeller, bearings, wearing rings, and seals

DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.16

Vapor bubbles collapse against the oncoming vane and cause a physical shock. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.12

"This physical shock creates small pits on the leading edge of the impeller vane." DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.12

Each pit is microscopic, but millions formed over hours or days can literally destroy an impeller. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.12

"Cavitation can also cause excessive pump vibration, which could damage pump bearings, wearing rings, and seals." DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.12
  • Increase the pressure at the suction of the pump
  • Reduce the temperature of the liquid being pumped
  • Reduce head losses in the pump suction piping
  • Reduce the flow rate through the pump
  • Reduce the speed of the pump impeller

DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.16

"Decreasing the temperature of the liquid decreases the saturation pressure, causing NPSHA to increase." DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.13
"Therefore, reducing the flow rate through a pump by throttling a discharge valve decreases NPSHR." DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.14

Head losses fall with a larger pipe diameter, fewer elbows, valves, and fittings, and a shorter pipe. A slower impeller also lowers NPSHR. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.13

Knowledge check: Recognizing and stopping cavitation

Objective 1.5Q1423

Which set lists the three indications of a cavitating pump?

The answer is B. The indications are noise, fluctuating discharge pressure and flow, and fluctuating pump motor current. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.12

Report a problem
Objective 1.6Q68

Which action helps stop cavitation in a centrifugal pump?

The answer is C. The handbook lists reducing liquid temperature as a step to stop cavitation; the other options reverse its listed steps of reducing flow rate, reducing impeller speed, and reducing suction head losses. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93, Centrifugal Pump Operation, ME-03 p. 16

Report a problem
Objective 1.6Q1424

Why does throttling a pump's discharge valve help stop cavitation?

The answer is B. Reducing the flow rate through a pump by throttling a discharge valve decreases NPSHR. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.14

Report a problem
Objective 1.7Q1425

What physical damage does cavitation do to an impeller?

The answer is B. The physical shock from collapsing bubbles creates small pits on the leading edge of the impeller vane. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.12

Gas binding and priming

Objectives 1.3

"Gas binding of a centrifugal pump is a condition where the pump casing is filled with gases or vapors to the point where the impeller is no longer able to contact enough fluid to function correctly." DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.15

The impeller spins in the gas bubble but cannot force liquid through the pump, which can lead to cooling problems for the packing and bearings. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.15

Pumps in systems with dissolved gases that are not self-venting should be periodically vented manually. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.15

"Most centrifugal pumps are not self-priming." DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.15

The casing must be filled with liquid before the pump is started. Most centrifugal pumps are located below the level of their suction source to stay primed. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.15

Characteristic curve, shutoff head, and runout

Objectives 1.3, 1.8, 1.9

At constant speed, flow through a centrifugal pump depends on the head it develops. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.14

"The lower the pump head, the higher the flow rate." DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.14
"Shutoff head is the maximum head that can be developed by a centrifugal pump operating at a set speed." DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.14
"Pump runout is the maximum flow that can be developed by a centrifugal pump without damaging the pump." DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.14
"A centrifugal pump is dead-headed when it is operated with no flow through it, for example, with a closed discharge valve or against a seated check valve." DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.15

With no flow path, the impeller churns the same liquid. Friction heats it until it flashes to vapor, which can interrupt cooling flow to the packing and bearings. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.15

"One method for protecting the pump from running dead-headed is to provide a recirculation line from the pump discharge line upstream of the discharge valve, back to the pump's supply source." DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.15

An automatic flow control device can also give this protection. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.15

"Runout can lead to cavitation and can also cause overheating of the pump's motor due to excessive currents." DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.15
"One method for ensuring that there is always adequate flow resistance at the pump discharge to prevent excessive flow through the pump is to place an orifice or a throttle valve immediately downstream of the pump discharge." DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.15

Properly designed piping systems are very important for runout protection. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.15

What is the shape of a centrifugal pump characteristic curve?

How is a centrifugal pump protected from dead-heading?

How is a centrifugal pump protected from runout?

Starting a centrifugal pump

From the lesson plan

"A centrifugal pump is started with the discharge valve throttled or closed to minimize the load on the impeller, allowing it to come up to speed quicker." Word: Pumps.docx, slide 1.44 Knowledge Check Centrifugal Pump Safety Precautions

This limits the amount of time that starting current exists. Word: Pumps.docx, slide 1.59 Centrifugal Pump Operation – Pump Startup

A motor that is not yet rotating has no counter-electromotive force, so it initially draws five to seven times the normal running current. Word: Pumps.docx, slide 1.63 Knowledge Check Operation of Centrifugal Pumps

Positive displacement pumps

Objectives 2.1, 2.2

"A positive displacement pump is one in which a definite volume of liquid is delivered for each cycle of pump operation." DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.18

That volume is constant regardless of the resistance to flow, within the limits of the driver and the pump's strength. A centrifugal pump, by contrast, delivers a continuous flow for any given speed and discharge resistance. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.18

"The three groups are reciprocating pumps, rotary pumps, and diaphragm pumps." DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.18
"The volume of liquid moved by the pump in one cycle (one suction stroke and one discharge stroke) is equal to the change in the liquid volume of the cylinder as the piston moves from its farthest left position to its farthest right position." DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.19

A simplex pump has one liquid cylinder, and a duplex pump is two simplex pumps side by side. A single-acting pump fills on one stroke and discharges on the return stroke. A double-acting pump fills one end of the cylinder while discharging the other. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.20

"Rotary pumps operate on the principle that a rotating vane, screw, or gear traps the liquid in the suction side of the pump casing and forces it to the discharge side of the casing." DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.22
"The simple gear pump shown in Figure 14 consists of two spur gears meshing together and revolving in opposite directions within a casing." DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.22
"It is considered as a simple gear pump having only two or three teeth per rotor; otherwise, its operation or the explanation of the function of its parts is no different." DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.24

Screw pumps trap liquid between intermeshing screws and slide it along the cylinder. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.25

"The screw pump is used for pumping viscous fluids, usually lubricating, hydraulic, or fuel oil." DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.25
"The rotor carries vanes that move in and out as it rotates to maintain sealed spaces between the rotor and the cylinder wall." DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.26
"The pump construction eliminates any contact between the liquid being pumped and the source of energy." DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.26

That eliminates the possibility of leakage, which matters for toxic or very expensive liquids. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.26

Objective 2.1Q1431

How does the flow of a positive displacement pump differ from a centrifugal pump?

The answer is B. The positive displacement pump delivers a definite volume of fluid for each cycle regardless of the head. Flow from a centrifugal pump depends on the head. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.18

Report a problem
Objective 2.2Q1432

A pump has two meshing spur gears revolving in opposite directions in a casing. What type is it?

The answer is C. The simple gear pump consists of two spur gears meshing together and revolving in opposite directions within a casing. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.22

Report a problem
Objective 2.2Q1433

A rotor carries vanes that move in and out to keep sealed spaces against the cylinder wall. What type of pump is it?

The answer is A. The rotor carries vanes that move in and out as it rotates to maintain sealed spaces between the rotor and the cylinder wall. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.26

Report a problem
Objective 2.2Q1434

What is the main benefit of a diaphragm pump?

The answer is C. The pump construction eliminates any contact between the liquid being pumped and the source of energy. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.26

Viscosity, curves, slippage, and protection

Objectives 2.3, 2.4, 2.5, 2.6

"In general, the effective flow rate of reciprocating pumps decreases as the viscosity of the fluid being pumped increases because the speed of the pump must be reduced." DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.21

As viscosity rises, the maximum speed at which a reciprocating pump can properly operate falls, so the maximum flow falls. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.28

"Therefore, the only factor that effects flow rate in an ideal positive displacement pump is the speed at which it operates." DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.27
"The characteristic curve for a positive displacement pump operating at a certain speed is a vertical line on a graph of head versus flow." DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.28

As discharge pressure rises, some liquid leaks from the discharge back to the suction, which reduces the effective flow rate. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.27

"Slippage is leakage of fluid from the discharge of the pump back to its suction." DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.22
"Positive displacement pumps are normally fitted with relief valves on the upstream side of their discharge valves to protect the pump and its discharge piping from overpressurization." DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.28

The relief valve prevents system and pump damage if the discharge valve is shut during operation or if anything else blocks system flow. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.28

Knowledge check: Viscosity, curves, slippage, and protection

Objective 2.3Q70

As the viscosity of the pumped liquid increases, the maximum speed at which a reciprocating positive displacement pump can properly operate:

The answer is A. The handbook says higher viscosity lowers both the maximum proper operating speed and the maximum flow rate. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93, Positive Displacement Pumps, ME-03 p. 28

Report a problem
Objective 2.4Q69

On a graph of head versus flow, the characteristic curve of a positive displacement pump operating at a set speed is:

The answer is A. The handbook says the curve is a vertical line, because the pump delivers a definite volume per cycle regardless of head; flow that falls with head describes a centrifugal pump in the same summary, and the other two shapes contradict the definite-volume behavior. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93, Positive Displacement Pumps, ME-03 p. 28

Report a problem
Objective 2.5Q1435

What is slippage in a positive displacement pump?

The answer is A. The rate at which liquid leaks from the pump discharge to its suction is called slippage. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.22

Report a problem
Objective 2.6Q345

Where is the overpressure relief valve for a positive displacement pump installed?

The answer is B. A PDP gives constant flow regardless of discharge pressure, so the relief valve sits upstream of the discharge isolation valve. DOE-1018-V1 (DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93), Positive Displacement Pumps, ME-03 p. 28

Report a problem
Objective 2.6Q344

How should a positive displacement pump's suction and discharge valves be positioned at startup?

The answer is D. A positive displacement pump should be started with both suction and discharge valves fully open. Approved lesson plan: Pumps (Pumps.docx), slide 1.91 Knowledge Check Reciprocating Positive-Displacement Pumps

Report a problem
Objective 2.4Q347

At constant speed, throttling closed a positive displacement pump's discharge valve makes flow ____ and pump head ____.

The answer is B. A PDP delivers constant flow over varying discharge pressure, while head rises as the head-loss curve shifts up. Approved lesson plan: Pumps (Pumps.docx), slide 1.111 Knowledge Check Characterisitc Curve for a PDP Pump

Annular linear induction pumps

From the lesson plan

"Annular Linear Induction Pumps are a type of electromagnetic pump used to move liquids without the need for any physical parts like impellers or rotating shafts." Word: ALIP Pumps.docx, slide 1.1 ALIP Intro

The parts of an ALIP are the coils, the outer core, the inner core, and the flow channel. Word: ALIP Pumps.docx, slide 1.3 ALIP Parts

"Motor action is achieved by having a current carrying conductor in a magnet field." Word: ALIP Pumps.docx, slide 1.4 ALIP, How It Works!

In an ALIP the liquid metal is that conductor. Electricity applied to the stator creates a magnetic field that pushes the liquid sodium, which acts as the rotor, through the channel. Word: ALIP Pumps.docx, slide 1.4 ALIP, How It Works!

"Note that since this design has stator windings on both sides of the channel an inner core of solid conductive material is needed to bridge the gap to maintain a strong magnetic field in the channel." Word: ALIP Pumps.docx, slide 1.3 ALIP Parts
  • Advantages: smaller and lighter, few or no moving parts, lower NPSH requirements, precise control of flow, and lower maintenance
  • Disadvantages: lower flow for a given power input, lower net efficiency at higher flows, and harder heat removal from the stator

Word: ALIP Pumps.docx, slide 1.4 ALIP, How It Works!

Worked examples

Objective 1.3,1.4

Checking for cavitation margin

A pump takes suction from an enclosed tank. Pa = 40 ft, Pst = 15 ft, hf = 5 ft, and Psat = 6 ft. The manufacturer gives NPSHR as 20 ft. Will the pump avoid cavitation?

  1. NPSHA = Pa + Pst - hf - Psat.
  2. NPSHA = 40 + 15 - 5 - 6 = 44 ft.
  3. Compare: 44 ft is greater than 20 ft, so NPSHA ≥ NPSHR is met.

Answer: Yes. NPSHA is 44 ft, which exceeds the 20 ft required.

DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.13

Summary

  • A centrifugal pump uses a rotating impeller and a volute or diffuser to convert velocity to pressure. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.10
  • Keep NPSHA at or above NPSHR to avoid cavitation, which shows as noise and fluctuating pressure, flow, and motor current. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.16
  • Protect against dead-heading with recirculation and against runout with an orifice or throttle valve. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.17
  • A positive displacement pump moves a definite volume each cycle and needs a relief valve upstream of its discharge valve. DOE-HDBK-1018/1-93 ME-03 p.28
  • An ALIP moves liquid metal with a magnetic field and has no impeller or rotating shaft. Word: ALIP Pumps.docx, slide 1.1 ALIP Intro
